title: Zurayid dynasty
capsule: The Zurayids were an Ismaili Shia dynasty ruling Aden and its hinterland in southern Yemen from c. 1083 to 1174, initially installed as vassals of the Sulayhid rulers of Sanaa. Their control of Aden made them the principal brokers of the Red Sea–Indian Ocean trade, with the port generating some 100,000 dinars annually in transit revenues. The dynasty maintained Fatimid allegiance and at times extended its authority northward to Taizz. Ayyubid general Turanshah conquered Aden on 22 June 1174, extinguishing the dynasty and incorporating its territory into Saladin's empire.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The dynasty's urban core at Aden is well documented in Islamic chronicles, but the extent of its rural and coastal hinterland is inferred from tribute records and remains imprecisely bounded.
